title: mcp.task.v1: an MCP Task, derived from a turn or a run
description: How the Control MCP server answers for a Task. A Task is not stored anywhere of its own: it is DERIVED, at the moment it is asked for, from the daemon's records and the event log, so it survives a restart of the MCP server and of the daemon. This record is that derivation; the server maps its fields onto the wire names of the protocol version it speaks (in the '2025-06-18' version the same facts are returned by the plain start, status and stop tools; in the '2026-07-28' version by the Tasks methods). task_id is the turn_id for work started with session.start or session.turn, and the run_id for work started with run.start. status is derived as follows. For a turn: queued or running with no approval pending -> 'working'; an approval pending for it -> 'input_required'; ended -> 'completed'; failed -> 'failed'; interrupted or stopped -> 'cancelled'. For a run: starting, running or unknown -> 'working' (an approval pending -> 'input_required'); ended with a result whose code is null -> 'completed'; ended with a result whose code is not null, start_failed, or lost_reboot -> 'failed'; stopped -> 'cancelled'. A cancel is a Stop: it answers 'pending' until the Stop is confirmed, and while it is pending the status stays as it was and cancel_requested is true. 'cancelled' is shown only after the Stop is confirmed (run.stop answered 'stopped'), never before. result is present exactly when the status is 'completed' or 'failed'; it is read from the event log's 'result' event. expires_at is when the Task can no longer be read; null means for as long as the daemon keeps the record, which today is for ever. An approval is never answered through a Task: 'input_required' tells the client that a person must answer on a surface that draws approvals.

task_id.description: A turn_id or a run_id, as 'of' says.

of.description: What the Task is derived from.

cancel_requested.description: True while a Stop has been asked and is not confirmed.

poll_interval_ms.description: How long a client should wait before asking again; null when the daemon gives no advice.

result.description: The payload of the 'result' event, plus the final text when there is one.
